When Triton stages the x_tile and w_tile through shared memory for tl.dot(), adjacent threads in the K-tile access memory locations separated by stride IN_C (e.g., 64, 128, 256, 512), which maps to different banks with a stride that is a multiple of 32 — the textbook bank-conflict pattern causing 16.1-way average conflicts. With this layout, adjacent K-lane threads differ by 1 in ic (stride-1 channel access), making shared memory accesses contiguous and bank-conflict-free. Both x_ptrs (NHWC, sx_c=1) and w_ptrs (OKHWI, sw_i=1) have channel as the innermost stride, so the new decode produces perfectly coalesced accesses.
